label: The hung hop is the manifest builder: ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs:51 imports buildManifestBytes from generate-leaf-manifest.cjs, so the pre-push skill gate's runtime is dominated by that builder's git calls.
generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:129 spawns git check-ignore -z --stdin with no timeout and no core.fsmonitor=false, so it takes the unbounded IPC path documented in iteration 2.
The existing fallback at generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:136 requires a returned result, so a hanging spawnSync never reaches it; adding a timeout alone makes the fallback reachable.

The repo already defines GIT_NO_FSMONITOR = [-c, core.fsmonitor=false] in check-source-tags-helper.mjs:53, cite-drift-scan.mjs:145 and continuity-freshness.ts:38; the hung path simply never adopted it.

Additional unbounded index-reading automation call sites: regenerate-skill-derived.cjs:73, verify-router-sync.cjs:168, doctor/git-hook-gates.cjs:180, doctor/release-update.cjs:282, sk-git/validate-message.mjs:88 and behavior-bench-run.cjs:885.

core.hooksPath is ~/.config/git/hooks, every entry symlinks into .skilled/scripts/git-hooks, and the skill gate is skippable only by SPECKIT_SKIP_PREPUSH_SKILL_GATE=1, so a timeout here fixes every machine checkout that trusts repo hooks.

Daemon-to-worktree attribution cannot use argv: every daemon runs exactly fsmonitor--daemon run --detach --ipc-threads=8 with no path, so the reaper must resolve the socket each process holds open instead.
Recovery must escalate past stop: because git fsmonitor--daemon stop polls forever on a wedged daemon, a reaper must bound the stop, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL.

Safest default is fsmonitor on only with worktrees outside the checkout, opted-out time-bounded automation and a daemon reaper; without all three, off for the main checkout via extensions.worktreeConfig and git config --worktree core.fsmonitor false.

Prevention invariant: no fsmonitor daemon may outlive its worktree and no automated git call may wait without a ceiling, enforced at worktree removal, in a stray-daemon reap and in a bounded wedge probe.

The highest-leverage single change is bounding and opting out the hook's check-ignore, which converts a wedged daemon into a fast gate warning through the existing fallback; relocation and reaping then remove the recurrence.
